title: Chronicling Change: 200 Years of Technological Milestones
html:
Chronicling Change: 200 Years of Technological Milestones

For years, I have been fascinated by the stories behind the technological innovations that shape our world. My recent thinking on this subject was (re-)sparked by several works (see below) which illustrated how seemingly isolated discoveries are often interconnected threads in a larger tapestry of progress. This interest sent me down a path of documenting technology milestones, with a general focus around digital, over the past 200 years and resulted in a personal research project: “Technological Milestones of the Past 200 Years.”

The report is a comprehensive compilation of the major technological milestones of the last two centuries. It is an exploration of the breakthroughs that have fundamentally reshaped how we live, from the foundational elements of computing and data storage to the rapid evolution of communication and software. Beyond just a list of dates and inventions, I have sought to capture some of the stories and dynamics of change that accompany these advancements.

History is not merely a recounting of the past; it is a vital tool for understanding the present and preparing for the future. I believe this compilation can serve as a public good to help us appreciate the ingenuity that drives technological transformation. It can be used to track innovation cycles, benchmark historical progress, identify interdependencies between technologies, and even help in forecasting future trends. 

I invite you to explore this resource in all its forms. In a spirit of collaboration, the report is not only available in PDF, but as a Google Document, a Google Spreadsheet, and a TimelineJS interactive. You can find everything on my website. I do not want my work locked behind a PDF, a fancy interactive, or an overly restrictive license. I want you to be able to download and use the data as needed.

I welcome your thoughts and collaboration as we continue to explore the ever-evolving story of human ingenuity.

Andrej

Books:

  • Map of Knowledge: How Classical Ideas Were Lost and Found: A History in Seven Cities by Violet Moller
  • Invention and Innovation: A Brief History of Hype and Failure by Vaclav Smil
  • The Innovators by Walter Isaacson
  • The Age of Heretics by Art Kleiner
  • Nexus: A Brief History of Information Networks from the Stone Age to AI by Yuval Noah Harari
